title: Stewardship
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Stewardship means faithfully managing what belongs to God, including time, gifts, money, body, opportunities, influence, and responsibilities. The believer owns nothing independently from the Lord.
summary: Stewardship means faithfully managing what belongs to God, including time, gifts, money, body, opportunities, influence, and responsibilities. The believer owns nothing independently from the Lord.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is Lord over the whole life, and His people are entrusted with resources to use for His kingdom. Faithful stewardship honors the Master who gives, entrusts, and will call His servants to account.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Everything belongs to God. The earth is the Lord’s, and believers are managers rather than ultimate owners. This changes how Christians view money, possessions, strength, time, gifts, and influence.

Stewardship requires faithfulness. God does not call His people to bury what He has entrusted to them in fear, laziness, or selfishness. He calls them to use what they have for His glory and the good of others.

Faithful stewardship also reaches small things. Jesus teaches that faithfulness in little matters. The ordinary use of resources reveals what the heart loves and trusts.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often treat life as personal property. Time is wasted, gifts are neglected, money is idolized, and opportunities are used for self rather than God.

This doctrine reminds believers that they will give account to the Lord. Stewardship is not guilt-driven pressure; it is grateful responsibility before the generous God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask what God has entrusted to you right now. Use your time, money, abilities, body, and influence with prayerful faithfulness. Give generously, serve wisely, avoid waste, and remember that every resource is a tool for worship and obedience.
